adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar interface requires createEvent(event, credentialId) but LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, BaseCalendarService and other implementations still declare a single parameter, causing TypeScript compilation failures across all implements Calendar classes
matched_golden_ids: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same interface-contract mismatch: Calendar.createEvent now requires (event, credentialId) but multiple implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365 and others) still define createEvent(event) with a single parameter, causing compilation/contract breakage across the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarManager.ts passes two arguments to createEvent implementations that accept one, causing type errors and silent ignoring of credentialId so destination selection only works for Google

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts`, the call was changed to `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. The `Calendar` type now expects `(event, credentialId)` (see `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts`), and GoogleCalendarService uses `credentialId` to pick the matching entry from the new `destinationCalendar: DestinationCalendar[]` array. However other implementations in the diff (e.g. `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) still define `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` and ignore the extra argument, and they select the calendar from only the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...`). With the new `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` looping over multiple `event.destinationCalendar` entries and passing a single shared `event` object, these non-Google services will keep using the first destination calendar rather than the one corresponding to the current credential/destination, leading to events created/updated in the wrong calendar(s). The finding’s “type errors” part isn’t verifiable here (TS can allow fewer params), but the silent ignoring / incorrect destination selection for non-Google is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GoogleCalendarService createEvent/updateEvent else-branch of selectedCalendar can never match because find only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, yielding calendarId: undefined and Google API 400/404 on updates and failed deletions when externalCalendarId is absent

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`, the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is falsy is now `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since `externalCalendarId` is falsy in that branch (likely `undefined`/`null`), the `find` predicate almost certainly never matches a real calendar `externalId`, yielding `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` as `undefined` (diff at `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent`). This can cause the Google API call to target an undefined calendarId unless there is an explicit fallback later (not shown in the diff), so the finding is a real defect for update/delete behavior when `externalCalendarId` is absent. (The finding’s mention of `createEvent` is not supported by the diff, but the core issue for update/delete is verifiable.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager updateEvent called with credential undefined when credentialId resolves to nothing, throwing TypeError and aborting reschedule for all remaining references in the loop
handleNewBooking evt.destinationCalendar?.push never runs when value is null, so a COLLECTIVE event whose organizer has no destination calendar silently drops all team hosts' destination calendars

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to either [eventType.destinationCalendar], [organizerUser.destinationCalendar], or null (if neither exists). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If the organizer (and eventType) has no destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null, so the optional-chained push is a no-op and the collected team hosts' destination calendars (built in `teamDestinationCalendars.push(user.destinationCalendar)`) are silently dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Prisma booking write only persists evt.destinationCalendar[0], so downstream readers only see a single calendar on read-back and multi-host persistence is not achieved

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `evt.destinationCalendar` is now treated as an array (e.g. team COLLECTIVE pushes multiple calendars), but when persisting the Booking it only connects the first element: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (handleNewBooking.ts). So any additional destination calendars in `evt.destinationCalendar` are not persisted on the Booking record and won’t be available on read-back (unless represented elsewhere, e.g. references). This is an incompleteness/scope concern rather than a verifiable runtime break in this diff because update/delete paths were also changed to rely on calendar references, not Booking.destinationCalendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: LarkCalendarService createEvent never receives credentialId and picks only the first destination calendar, so multi-host collective events are always written to host #1's Lark calendar only, same for Office365

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over each destination calendar and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. However, `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` and `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` still derive the target calendar from only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then use its `externalId`), and they do not select a destination calendar based on the credential being used (unlike `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, which now finds by `credentialId`). As a result, when creating events for multiple destination calendars/hosts, Lark/Office365 will always target the first destination calendar rather than the one corresponding to the current credential, causing events to be written to the wrong calendar or fail for other hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:253-256 dead fallback branch: when externalCalendarId is falsy, the find() searching for externalId === undefined always returns undefined, causing calendarId: undefined to be passed to the API so updates/deletes silently fail for bookings lacking externalCalendarId

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, updateEvent/deleteEvent changed the fallback from using a known destination calendar externalId to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined). If `externalCalendarId` is not provided, this `find()` compares against null/undefined and will typically return undefined even when `event.destinationCalendar` contains valid calendars, so the code loses the intended fallback calendarId selection (and in updateEvent can result in an undefined/incorrect calendarId being used). This is a real behavioral regression exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule.handler.ts:237-240 dropped the user.destinationCalendar fallback, so reschedule requests for bookings without per-booking destination calendars construct events with destinationCalendar: [] unlike all sibling handlers

adjudication.rationale: In requestReschedule.handler.ts the pre-change code already had no user.destinationCalendar fallback: it was `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` (a duplicate), so the diff did not “drop” a user fallback. The change does set destinationCalendar to `[]` when bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar is missing, but that behavior is not a regression from an existing user fallback in this file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:166-168 references from the no-credentialId branch set externalCalendarId only from result.externalId, but createEvent returns undefined when no third argument is passed, storing references with externalCalendarId: undefined which triggers the dead-fallback bug

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents(), when iterating destination calendars that lack credentialId, it calls createEvent(c, event) without passing the destination externalId (see the branch that filters credentials by `c.type === destination.integration`). CalendarManager.createEvent returns an EventResult containing `externalId` from that third argument, so it will be `undefined` in this branch. Later, EventManager maps calendar results to references using `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` (around the shown 164-205 area), meaning references for those created events will store `externalCalendarId: undefined` even though a destination calendar externalId exists. This is a concrete behavioral defect introduced by the refactor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:1073-1075 uses ?.push on null evt.destinationCalendar, silently dropping all collective team calendars when the organizer has none; should assign a new array instead

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, collective team calendars are added via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If it is a COLLECTIVE team event and the organizer has no destination calendar, this optional-chained push is a no-op, so `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently dropped. The finding matches the diff and indicates broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Touched CalendarEvent-construction paths (bookingReminder.ts, confirm.handler.ts, webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts) omit hideCalendarNotes, so attendee notes are written in plain text to the organizer's calendar despite the hide setting

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows multiple CalendarEvent objects being constructed/modified (e.g., confirm.handler.ts, packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, bookingReminder.ts) where only destinationCalendar handling was updated, but hideCalendarNotes is not set from booking/eventType. Since CalendarManager.createEvent enforces note-hiding only when calEvent.hideCalendarNotes is truthy (it overwrites additionalNotes), these flows would bypass the hide behavior if they create/update calendar events after confirmation/payment. The finding overreaches slightly by including bookingReminder.ts (which in the shown snippet just emails), but the core issue (missing hideCalendarNotes propagation in touched CalendarEvent construction paths that likely lead to calendar writes) is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests verify the new behavior: nothing asserts collective bookings create one calendar event per host destination or that the DB-credential fallback works; the only test change is a fixture literal fix

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new behavior (e.g., EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now iterates over event.destinationCalendar[] and, for each destination, may fetch a missing credential via prisma.credential.findUnique before calling createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId); similarly update workflow now processes multiple calendar references and can also DB-fetch missing credentials). However, the only test change shown is in apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts changing a fixture literal from destinationCalendar: null to destinationCalendar: [], with no new assertions covering: (1) collective/team behavior that pushes multiple destination calendars (handleNewBooking adds teamDestinationCalendars for COLLECTIVE and pushes into evt.destinationCalendar), or (2) the DB-credential fallback paths added in EventManager and handleCancelBooking. This is a concrete missing-test gap for newly added multi-calendar + DB fallback logic, not a direct functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts:449-56 recurring-cancellation loop uses find to pick only the first calendar reference per booking, leaving orphaned events on other hosts' calendars for recurring collective bookings

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, even after changing the top-level selection to `filter` and iterating `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`, the recurring-cancellation branch still uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` inside the loop over `updatedBookings`. If a recurring collective booking produces multiple `_calendar` references per booking (consistent with this PR’s shift to `destinationCalendar` as an array and multi-calendar refs elsewhere), `find` will only delete the first calendar event per `updBooking`, leaving additional calendar events undeleted (orphaned) on other hosts/calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated inversion of IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED slug-conditioning in create.handler.ts:150-153 silently changes organization-slug persistence behavior on non-team-billing deployments, unrelated to PR intent
loadUsers rewrite drops organization.slug include, causing user.organization.slug to be undefined and breaking org-prefixed routing for dynamic-link bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the `loadUsers` rewrite removes the explicit `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the `prisma.user.findMany({ select: ... })` query (it existed before, now it’s gone). This can cause `user.organization?.slug` to be missing for dynamically loaded users unless `userSelect.select` already includes it (not shown in the diff). The claimed downstream break (“org-prefixed routing for dynamic-link bookings”) is plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New empty-dynamicUserList guard in loadUsers turns previously-working calls with empty lists into a 500 error where old code returned []

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, `loadUsers` was changed to throw when `!eventTypeId` and `dynamicUserList` is not an array or is empty: `if (!Array.isArray(dynamicUserList) || dynamicUserList.length === 0) { throw new Error(...) }`. That error is caught and rethrown as `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })` (since it’s not an `HttpError` or `PrismaClientKnownRequestError`). Previously, the code called `prisma.user.findMany({ where: { username: { in: dynamicUserList }}})` which, for an empty `in: []`, would return `[]` (no users) rather than a 500. This is a behavior regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamEventType rewrite replaces SchedulingType enum comparison with magic string-array includes check, weakening type-safety and introducing unrelated churn

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, `isTeamEventType` was changed from enum comparisons (`eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE || ...ROUND_ROBIN`) to `!!eventType.schedulingType && ["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`. This replaces type-safe enum usage with magic strings, making the check less robust to enum/value changes and adding scope-unrelated churn in a PR primarily about `destinationCalendar` becoming an array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule.handler.ts:240-243 drops the user.destinationCalendar fallback, sending [] for bookings whose only destinationCalendar is on the user, losing calendar context in reschedule flows

adjudication.rationale: In `requestReschedule.handler.ts` the pre-change code already had no `user.destinationCalendar` fallback: it was `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` (a redundant self-fallback). The diff changes this to `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar] : []`, which does not “drop” a `user.destinationCalendar` fallback because none existed in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback expression is dead code: find predicate compares externalId to undefined/null and always returns undefined, so API calls proceed with undefined calendarId

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. But that branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, so the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and will almost always return `undefined`, causing the code to fall back to the default calendar ("primary") instead of the intended destination calendar. The finding’s “undefined calendarId” phrasing is off (the code falls back to "primary"), but the core issue (broken/dead fallback logic) is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking constructs destinationCalendar as null while other call sites use [], creating inconsistent null vs [] invariant across the DestinationCalendar[] | null type

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events it tries to append team member destination calendars via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If `destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional chaining prevents the push, so collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently dropped. This is a real behavioral defect tied to using `null` instead of an empty array (most other call sites now normalize to `[]`), and it can prevent creating calendar events for team members in that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated spelling change from 'organiser' to 'organizer' in CalendarManager.ts changes a user-visible string with no requirement

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a spelling change in `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` from "organiser" to "organizer" in the user-facing string `calEvent.additionalNotes = "Notes have been hidden by the organizer";`. However, this is a minor wording/locale variant change and not a verifiable defect or an important review issue grounded in the diff (no behavior is broken, and the claim about “no requirement” cannot be verified from the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated typo fix renaming orginalBookingDuration to originalBookingDuration is unrelated churn mixed into the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include a typo-only rename in `handleNewBooking.ts` (`orginalBookingDuration` -> `originalBookingDuration`). That’s a cosmetic refactor with no behavior change, and calling it “unrelated churn” is essentially a style/scope nit rather than a specific defect or substantive review issue grounded in correctness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:117 - mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws TypeError when evt.destinationCalendar is [] or null because destructured first element is undefined and dereferenced without guard, crashing event creation for users booking Google Meet with no destination calendar instead of falling back to Daily
matched_golden_ids: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same root cause: evt.destinationCalendar can be null or an empty array, so destructuring the first element yields undefined, and then accessing a property on mainHostDestinationCalendar causes a TypeError/null reference during event creation (and by implication similar paths). This matches the golden issue about undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar due to null/empty destinationCalendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:253 (and ~315) - else-branch find comparing cal.externalId against falsy externalCalendarId is dead code always evaluating to undefined, so updateEvent sends calendarId: undefined to Google API when no externalCalendarId passed; replaced previous working fallback event.destinationCalendar?.externalId; same pattern duplicated in deleteEvent

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar id as `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that else-branch `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, so the `.find(...)` predicate almost always fails and returns `undefined`, breaking the previous working fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (now array-based). This can lead to updating/deleting against an undefined/incorrect calendar id (or falling back to `primary` if later code does so), rather than the intended destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create.handler.ts:151-153 - ternary rewrite inverts original boolean logic: IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {} sets slug when billing is enabled (opposite of old !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }), breaking slug-approval workflow with inverted requestedSlug metadata

This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same boolean logic inversion: slug is now set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true (opposite of the original behavior). It also references requestedSlug/metadata being inverted, aligning with the golden note that the combination causes incorrect slug/requestedSlug states under enabled/disabled billing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:~530 - update path calls updateEvent(credential, ...) without guarding for undefined credential when reference.credentialId is set but credential not found, so dangling/deleted credential crashes reschedule with unhandled TypeError instead of recording failed EventResult
matched_golden_ids: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same scenario: updateEvent is called with a potentially undefined credential when reference.credentialId exists but the credential lookup fails, leading to a runtime TypeError/crash. This matches the golden comment's concern about guarding/handling undefined credentials to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule.handler.ts:240 - bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar compares operand to itself and drops user.destinationCalendar fallback kept in sibling paths, so users with no booking-level destination calendar get destinationCalendar: [] and reschedule-request flows lose the calendar

adjudication.rationale: In requestReschedule.handler.ts the new assignment `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []` only considers the booking-level destination calendar and otherwise forces an empty array. Unlike multiple sibling paths in this diff (e.g., confirm/editLocation/payments) that fall back to `user.destinationCalendar`, this reschedule flow has no such fallback, so users without a booking-level destination calendar will lose the destination calendar in the reschedule request event payload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:119-125 - organizer email taken from first element of destinationCalendar while event is inserted into credential-matched calendar, so for collective events with multiple Google hosts, host #2's calendar gets organizer.email = host #1's externalId, causing Google to reject or misattribute the organizer

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts#createEvent`, the insert `calendarId` is chosen by matching `credentialId` against `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` (`find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`), but the organizer attendee `email` is taken from `mainHostDestinationCalendar`, which is always the *first* element of `destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...`). With multiple destination calendars (collective/team case), creating the event for host/credential #2 will still set organizer.email based on host #1’s destination calendar externalId, creating a mismatch between the calendar being written and the organizer identity derived from `destinationCalendar[0]`. This is a concrete inconsistency introduced by the array refactor and could plausibly cause Google API misattribution/rejection depending on what `externalId` represents.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:~1874 - Booking row stores only destinationCalendar[0] while CalendarEvent array holds every collective host's calendar, so booking.destinationCalendar is a lossy projection and downstream consumers (cancel, reminders, webhooks) see only the organizer's calendar, creating a drifting second source of truth vs references

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `evt.destinationCalendar` is now an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, additional host destination calendars are pushed (`handleNewBooking.ts`: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the Booking row, only the first element is connected (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), meaning the Booking model still stores a single `destinationCalendar` while the in-memory `CalendarEvent` may carry multiple. Many downstream event reconstructions still derive `destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar` and wrap it into a single-element array (e.g., `bookingReminder.ts`, payment webhooks), so those code paths will not reflect all collective hosts’ calendars. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded inconsistency/second-source-of-truth concern, though the diff also updates cancellation/deletion/update logic to use calendar references arrays, so it’s not strictly verifiable as an immediate functional break from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:344-370 - credential-from-DB fetch + mapping block (prisma.credential.findUnique → hand-built CredentialWithAppName) is duplicated verbatim in update path at ~line 510; should be extracted to a resolveCredential(id) helper to avoid divergence

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new prisma.credential.findUnique() fallback when a credential isn’t found in memory, followed by a manual mapping into a CredentialWithAppName shape in EventManager.ts inside createAllCalendarEvents (around the new loop over destinationCalendar). A very similar fallback + hand-built mapping block is also added in the update path (inside the loop over calendar references) when reference.credentialId is present but not found in this.calendarCredentials. This is duplicated logic that could diverge over time and is reasonably extractable into a helper like resolveCredential(id). It’s a maintainability/architecture concern rather than a directly broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create.handler.ts:148-151 condition inverted: slug is now set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is enabled instead of disabled, causing organizations to be created without a slug when team billing is disabled

adjudication.rationale: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts the condition controlling slug assignment was inverted: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Now when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false, neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug` is set, so organizations can be created without any slug at all under the non-team-billing path, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: requestReschedule.handler.ts:237-240 drops the fallback to user's destination calendar, producing an empty destination calendar for legacy bookings on reschedule

adjudication.rationale: In requestReschedule.handler.ts the pre-change code was `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar`, which never provided a fallback to the user’s destination calendar (it ORs the same value). The new code returns `[bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar]` or `[]`, but it does not “drop” a user fallback because no such fallback existed in the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:358-365 omits destination.externalId, so the no-credentialId path always falls back to 'primary' instead of the configured external calendar

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents(), when iterating destination calendars, the branch where `destination.credentialId` is missing falls back to creating events for all matching credentials but calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing the destination’s `externalId` (unlike the `credentialId` branch which calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`). Since CalendarManager.createEvent returns `externalId` on the EventResult and EventManager later uses `result.externalId` to populate `externalCalendarId`, this omission means the created calendar reference won’t carry the configured external calendar id. For Google specifically, `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` selects the calendar by matching `destinationCalendar[].credentialId`; with no credentialId present it yields `undefined` and falls back to `"primary"`. So the no-credentialId path will not reliably use the configured external calendar and can default to primary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:253-256 and :312-315 fallback branch is dead code: find(cal => cal.externalId === falsy) never matches, so update/delete without externalCalendarId pass undefined as calendarId causing API failures

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute a fallback calendar id as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the fallback branch), the `find` predicate becomes `cal.externalId === undefined/null`, which will not match normal destination calendars (they have real `externalId`s). So the fallback cannot select any destination calendar and yields `undefined`, changing behavior from the prior `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback and potentially causing updates/deletes to target the wrong calendar (e.g., default/primary) or fail if the event is not in primary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:1060-1066 persists only the first destination calendar on the booking row, so downstream readers (reminders, webhooks, reschedule, cancel) drop other collective hosts' calendars

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the PR builds `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, appends additional hosts’ destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the booking it only connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id` to the booking (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), meaning only the first destination calendar is stored on the booking row. Downstream code shown in this diff often reconstructs `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (wrapping it into a single-element array), so any additional collective hosts’ destination calendars added to `evt` are not persisted/recoverable from the booking record and will be absent from those later flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:87-91 hardcodes organizer email to destinationCalendar[0].externalId, so secondary hosts' events show the first host's calendar email as organizer

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the organizer attendee email is set from `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (the first element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar`) via `email: mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId ? mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId : calEventRaw.organizer.email`. However, the calendar actually used for insertion is chosen per-credential (`destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`). When creating events for multiple destination calendars/credentials (see `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` looping over `event.destinationCalendar`), secondary hosts’ events can be inserted into their own calendar but still have the organizer email taken from destinationCalendar[0], i.e., the first host’s calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB credential lookup without ownership scope: prisma.credential.findUnique fetches any credential without userId/teamId filter, allowing cross-tenant calendar writes using other users' OAuth credentials if credentialId can be influenced by non-owners

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple new `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: ... } })` lookups without scoping by `userId`/`teamId` before using the returned credential to create/update/delete calendar events. Examples: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` fetches by `destination.credentialId` and then calls `createEvent(credential, event, ...)`; `EventManager.updateCalendarEvent` similarly fetches by `reference.credentialId` and then calls `updateEvent(...)`; `handleCancelBooking` fetches by `credentialId` from booking references and then calls `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`. If a non-owner-influenced `credentialId` ever reaches these paths (e.g., via references/destinationCalendar), this can result in cross-tenant use of another user's OAuth credentials. The lack of ownership/tenant filtering is verifiable in the diff and is a security correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted org-slug gating in create.handler.ts: slug is now assigned directly when billing is enabled (opposite of previous behavior), letting unverified orgs claim any slug immediately, bypassing the requestedSlug approval flow

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the conditional spread for `slug` was flipped: it changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Previously, when team billing was enabled, the slug was not set directly and instead `metadata.requestedSlug` was set; now when billing is enabled the org record gets `slug` immediately (and also sets `requestedSlug`). This matches the finding that the approval/request flow can be bypassed for billing-enabled org creation compared to prior behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendees' full destinationCalendar rows including credentialId are propagated into evt for COLLECTIVE events, flowing into emails, serialization, originalEvent, and error logs instead of being reduced to only what the calendar layer needs

adjudication.rationale: The diff does propagate full `DestinationCalendar` objects (likely including `credentialId` and other DB fields) into `evt.destinationCalendar` for COLLECTIVE team events: `handleNewBooking.ts` collects `teamDestinationCalendars: DestinationCalendar[]` by pushing `user.destinationCalendar` and then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. That `evt` is then passed through layers that log/return the full `calEvent` object (e.g., `CalendarManager.createEvent` logs `calEvent` on failure and returns `originalEvent: calEvent` in the `EventResult`), and email/template code reads from `calEvent.destinationCalendar` (e.g., `BrokenIntegrationEmail.tsx`). The finding’s concern is therefore grounded (data minimization/architecture), but the diff alone doesn’t prove an actual external leak via emails/webhooks/serialization, so it’s better classified as a non-bug review issue rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Snapshot fixture update in webhook.e2e.ts (destinationCalendar: null -> []) is a mechanical accommodation, with no test verifying that a collective booking produces one calendar event per host's destination calendar, correct externalId per credential, or per-destination reference storage

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a mechanical snapshot adjustment in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts` (`destinationCalendar: null` -> `[]`) to match the refactor where `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` became an array. At the same time, substantial new behavior was added: `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over multiple destination calendars and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, and `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` selects the calendar by matching `credentialId`. No corresponding assertions/tests are added in this diff to validate the new multi-destination/collective behavior (one event per host destination, correct externalId-per-credential routing, and reference storage), beyond updating the snapshot shape.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts updateEvent fallback branch is tautological: the find predicate can never match when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always yields undefined (same pattern in deleteEvent ~line 312)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the fallback branch), the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId` to the same falsy `externalCalendarId` (likely `undefined`/`null`), so it will almost always return `undefined` and fail to fall back to any destination calendar. The same faulty pattern is used in `deleteEvent` when computing `calendarId` (and also `selectedCalendar` there), making the fallback effectively non-functional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: loadUsers wrapper in handleNewBooking.ts converts the guard's own thrown Error into a 500 HttpError because plain Error doesn't match the instanceof checks, causing a status-code mismatch with the intended 400

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the new `loadUsers` wrapper throws plain `Error` for input/shape guards (e.g., `throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` and `throw new Error("eventType.hosts is not properly defined.")`). The surrounding `catch` only maps `HttpError` or `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` to a 400; all other errors (including these guard `Error`s) are converted into `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`. This makes client/input validation failures return 500 instead of the likely intended 400.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lark CalendarService createEvent changed to use only the first element of destinationCalendar, silently dropping every non-first host's Lark calendar in collective bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`, meaning it always uses only the first destination calendar in the array. However, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` was changed to iterate over `event.destinationCalendar` and call `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination. Since the same `event` object (with a multi-entry `destinationCalendar` array) is passed on each iteration, the Lark service will still select the first entry’s `externalId` for every Lark credential invocation, causing non-first hosts’ Lark calendars to be ignored/mis-targeted (events created in the wrong calendar or failing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateAllCalendarEvents in EventManager.ts has no test for the new credential-from-DB branch or the case where reference.credentialId resolves to no credential, causing updateEvent(undefined, ...) to throw with no assertion on the result shape or count

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts, the refactored calendar-reference loop calls `updateEvent(credential, event, ...)` even when `credential` may still be `undefined`. Specifically, inside `if (reference.credentialId)`, it sets `credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0];` and if not found it tries `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)`, but there is no guard after that fetch—`result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` runs regardless. If the DB lookup returns null (or app slug missing), `credential` remains undefined and `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` will throw. This defect is introduced/exposed by the new credential-from-DB branch and the missing existence check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback is dead code: when externalCalendarId is null, find() matches nothing and returns undefined, causing calendar.events.update/delete to be called with calendarId: undefined and Google rejecting the call, breaking cancellation of pre-migration bookings

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is `null/undefined`, the `find` predicate compares against `externalCalendarId` (still `undefined`), so it will return `undefined` in normal cases. The subsequent `calendar.events.update(...)` uses `selectedCalendar` (no `|| "primary"` fallback shown like in `createEvent`), meaning the Google API call can be made with `calendarId: undefined` and fail. The same pattern was introduced in `deleteEvent` (`calendarId` computed via a `find` against `externalCalendarId` when it’s falsy), making the intended fallback effectively non-functional in the falsy-`externalCalendarId` path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:117 unguarded array element access crashes with TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty array for Meet-location events, affecting cancel/reschedule/reminder flows

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the diff changes the safe optional-chaining check `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` to array destructuring and then direct property access: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []; if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar") ...`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `[]` (which this diff introduces in multiple flows, e.g. bookingReminder/payments/cancel handlers now set `destinationCalendar: ... ? [selected] : []`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` will throw a TypeError for Meet-location events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:1874 persists only the first host's destination calendar for collective events, losing other hosts' calendars for subsequent DB-reconstructed flows with no way to re-derive the data

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, for collective team events the code explicitly accumulates additional hosts' destination calendars into `evt.destinationCalendar` (via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), but when persisting the booking it only connects the first element: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }` (around the shown change near line ~1874). This drops any additional destination calendars from persistence, so later flows that rebuild `CalendarEvent` from the stored booking’s `destinationCalendar` (which remains singular) cannot recover the extra hosts’ calendars from the booking record.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:253-258 updateEvent: fallback branch uses externalCalendarId (falsy) to find a matching calendar, so find never matches and calendarId is undefined, causing Google API rejection for bookings without externalCalendarId

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback branch is now:
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (undefined), so it will almost always return `undefined`, making `selectedCalendar` undefined. This is a regression from the previous logic (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and can lead to calling Google `events.update` with an undefined `calendarId` (unless later code provides a default), matching the finding’s described failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts:312-315 deleteEvent: same undefined calendarId bug on the fallback path, causing the calendar event delete to fail

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the fallback path for `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, the `.find(... externalCalendarId)` predicate compares against `undefined`, so it will typically return `undefined` even if `event.destinationCalendar` contains valid calendars. That can yield an undefined `calendarId` on the fallback path (previously it would use `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), causing the delete call to target an invalid/undefined calendar id unless there is an additional fallback later (not shown in the diff). The same pattern also appears in `updateEvent` selection logic, reinforcing that this is a real bug introduced by the refactor to an array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:~1066-1071: evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...) silently no-ops when destinationCalendar is null, dropping all team members' destination calendars for COLLECTIVE events with no error or warning

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. Because of optional chaining, this is a silent no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, so any collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped with no error. This matches the finding and is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts:~430-465: recurring-event branch iterates all credentials for each reference, producing N×M duplicate deleteEvent calls for the same uids, with the second delete failing and producing spurious errors and inflated apiDeletes results

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the new logic sets `bookingCalendarReference` to an array (`filter(...)`) and then loops `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside the `if (credentialId)` recurring-event branch, it still builds `promises` by iterating **all** `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(..._calendar)` and for each credential iterates `updatedBookings` and deletes each `bookingRef` UID (`calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)`, where `uid` comes from `updBooking.references.find(...)`). Because this recurring deletion loop does not use the outer `reference.uid` and is executed once per `reference`, having multiple calendar references will repeat the same deletes N times (references × credentials × updatedBookings), causing duplicate delete attempts for the same UIDs and inflated `apiDeletes`/spurious errors as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts: delete failures are only logged, never surfaced to the user, who sees 'booking cancelled' while some remote events may fail to delete

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, calendar deletion in the recurring-event branch wraps `await Promise.all(promises)` in a try/catch that only logs (`logger.error(error.message)`) and does not rethrow or otherwise affect control flow, so the handler can proceed even if remote deletes fail. The diff does not show any mechanism that would propagate these failures back to the caller/user from this catch path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:~500-525 updateAllCalendarEvents: if prisma.credential.findUnique returns null, updateEvent is still called with undefined credential, throwing a TypeError that aborts the loop, skipping remaining calendar references and reporting all as failed with credentialId: 0

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts updateAllCalendarEvents (shown around the ~493+ block), inside `for (const reference of calendarReference)`, when `reference.credentialId` is present it sets `credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0]` and, if falsy, tries `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` to reconstruct it. However, regardless of whether a credential is found/reconstructed, it unconditionally executes `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));`. If `findUnique` returns null (or lacks `app.slug`), `credential` remains undefined and `updateEvent` is called with undefined, which will throw and be caught by the outer try/catch, aborting the loop and causing the catch block to report failures for all references (credentialId: 0). This matches the finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:~360 createAllCalendarEvents: if the DB fetch for a credential fails, the destination is silently skipped with no event created and no error, while the booking still reports success

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new loop over `event.destinationCalendar` attempts to resolve a credential either from `this.calendarCredentials` or via `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)`. If neither yields a `credential` (e.g., DB fetch returns null, missing `app.slug`, etc.), the code simply does nothing for that `destination` (no `else` branch, no error/log, no failed `EventResult`), so that destination calendar gets no event created without any explicit failure signal from this function. However, the claim that “the booking still reports success” isn’t directly verifiable from this diff alone (it depends on downstream handling of an empty/partial `createdEvents` array).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:~556: non-awaited updateEvent push inside loop combined with Promise.all causes one rejecting updateEvent to collapse all per-reference results into a blanket failure with no record of which calendars were actually updated

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts the refactor changes `calendarReference` from a single reference to an array and iterates it, doing `result.push(updateEvent(...))` per reference inside a `try`. The surrounding `catch` now returns a blanket failure array for *all* references (`calendarReference?.map(...)`), losing per-calendar success/failure detail. If the (likely existing, but not shown in the diff hunk) code later does `return await Promise.all(result)` (common pattern with this `result` array), a single rejecting `updateEvent` would throw and trigger that `catch`, collapsing partial successes into all-failed. This risk is specifically introduced by the new multi-reference loop + blanket failure catch behavior.
